state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.text: Let's focus on the misconception that changing all values by the same proportion won't affect the range. Can you think about how cutting all the plants in half or growing them by the same amount might impact the range? This can help us understand why the range may or may not change in these situations.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess if we cut all the plants in half, the heights would still be in the same order, so maybe the range would stay the same? But I'm not sure about Katie's idea. If we add \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) to each height, wouldn't that change the highest and lowest values? How does that affect the range?
